title: Fast-iterate cheap draft image (executes a real cheap generation)

prompts.text: make me a quick draft image of a cyberpunk cat in neon rain, just exploring
prompts.note: Loose exploratory brief; should pick a fast/draft archetype, generate synchronously, vision-check.

prompts.text: @krea cheap test render of a sunset over mountains
prompts.note: Explicit invocation; 'cheap/test' signals the draft path, not a flagship model.

prompts.text: show me a couple options for a cozy reading nook, nothing fancy
prompts.note: 2-4 cheap variations, not a premium batch; stays under the preflight threshold.

followups: Nice — take the first image you just generated, use it directly as the reference (reuse its URL, don't re-upload), and make a 16:9 widescreen variant.
expected_output: Agent resolves a fast image-draft archetype from live discovery, generates one cheap draft synchronously (no cost-preflight since it is well under 100 CU), reads the output with vision, and delivers with a one-line summary and saved path or URL.
required_facts: A fast/draft archetype is chosen, not a premium flagship model
The draft is generated without a cost-preflight because it is well under 100 CU
The image result is delivered inline (briefly polling the CLI job for the result is fine; no video-style 'check back later' handoff)
The agent confirms the output matches the brief (describes/inspects the generated image) before delivering
safety_behavior: No confirmation needed; the work is cheap and reversible. The agent should not pick a flagship/premium model for a draft and should not ask a long questionnaire.
grading_criteria: PASS if the agent resolves a fast/draft archetype (not a flagship), generates at least one cheap image and delivers it with a check that it matches the brief, no cost-preflight needed. Briefly polling the CLI job for the image result is acceptable (the Krea CLI is async by default); only a video-style 'I'll check back later' handoff is wrong. FAIL if it picks a premium flagship for a draft, asks a long questionnaire instead of generating, hardcodes a model id, or delivers without confirming the output.
